lessons.title: mein, dein, sein…
lessons.summary: Words for 'my, your, his, her…'. They take the same endings as ein.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Talking about your job, your colleagues and your family: **Mein Chef ist nett.** **Ihre Firma ist in Hamburg.** **Unsere Kollegin heißt Sara.**

cards.title: One for each person
cards.body: Each personal pronoun has its possessive. Careful: **sein** = his/its, **ihr** = her **and** their, **Ihr** (capital) = your (polite).

cards.title: Endings like ein
cards.body: The ending depends on the **noun** that follows, just like ein/eine. Feminine and plural add **-e**; masculine in the accusative adds **-en**.
cards.tip: euer loses an e with an ending: eure Firma.

cards.title: his or her?
cards.body: The possessive depends on the **owner**, the ending on the **thing**. Tom and his car: **sein** Auto. Lisa and her car: **ihr** Auto. Lisa and her computer: **ihr** Computer.

examples.german: Herr Klein arbeitet viel. **Seine** Arbeit ist interessant.
examples.english: Mr Klein works a lot. His work is interesting.
Mrs Roth is looking for her key.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'meine Chef': der Chef → **mein** Chef. Not 'sein Auto' for a woman: **ihr** Auto. And polite **Ihr** has a capital I.

games.prompt: Match the pronoun and its possessive
games.explanation: Each person has its own possessive.

games.prompt: Lisa talks about her… : ihr or ihre?
games.explanation: Feminine and plural add -e, like eine.
Paul is the owner (sein), Chefin is feminine (+e): seine.

lessons.title: mit, ohne, als, wie
lessons.summary: Small words that say how, with what and in what role: mit dem Bus, ohne Pause, als Lehrer, wie ein Profi.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: Describing your job and how you work: **Ich arbeite als Krankenpfleger.** **Ich fahre mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit.** **Ich arbeite ohne Pause.**

cards.title: als = as (a role)
cards.body: **als** + profession, without article: your role at work. Don't confuse it with **wie**, which compares.

examples.german: Ich arbeite **als** Kellner in einem Café.
examples.english: I work as a waiter in a café.

cards.tip: als = what you are, wie = what you are similar to.

cards.title: mit = with / by
cards.body: **mit** says who you're with, what you use and how you travel. It's always followed by the **dative**: dem (der/das), der (die), den + n (plural).

cards.title: ohne = without
cards.body: **ohne** is the opposite of mit, but takes the **accusative** and very often no article at all.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'Ich arbeite wie Lehrerin' for your job: **als** Lehrerin. Not 'mit der Bus': **mit dem Bus**. And no article after als.

examples.german: Ich fahre **mit der** U-Bahn ins Büro.
examples.english: I take the underground to the office.

games.explanation: als for a role, wie for a comparison.
der/das → dem, die → der, plural → den + n.
